model.name: Product Type / Catalog Item
model.purpose: Govern the class-level catalog item (trade-item type) that uniquely identifies a product or service as ordered, priced or invoiced, independently of any serialised instance and independently of any commercial offer, price or availability statement.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the master-data identity, classification, type-level specification, packaging hierarchy, variant grouping, lifecycle, ownership, regulatory type identifiers, typed relationships and catalog evidence of a product type / catalog item. It is the GTIN-class (or equivalent class-level key) that classifies item instances and that engineering BOMs compose; it is not the instance, not the lot, and not the offer.
in_scope: Class-level trade-item identification (GTIN-8/12/13/14 and canonical GS1 Digital Link URI without serial or lot qualifiers) and equivalent type keys (MPN plus brand, SKU as merchant type key, NSN, ISBN-as-GTIN-13, ASIN as marketplace type key).

Type-level naming, brand, description, language, declared net content, formulation/functionality, physical dimensions and other characteristic data that apply identically to all occurrences of the class.
Classification of the type in GPC, UNSPSC, Harmonized System, and property-bearing industrial dictionaries (IEC 61360 / eCl@ss / ISO 22745 open technical dictionaries).

Variant grouping (ProductGroup / ProductModel / isVariantOf), packaging-hierarchy GTINs (unit, inner pack, case, pallet trade-item levels), and type-level accessory, spare, similar and consumable links.

Catalog-item lifecycle: new-product GTIN assignment, attribute-change rules that force a new GTIN, discontinuation/withdrawal, identifier non-reuse, predecessor/successor, and draft/investigational status.
Brand-owner / GTIN-allocator authority, manufacturer and device-labeler roles, type-level certifications, and medical-device UDI-DI / Basic UDI-DI (GMN) as type (not production) identifiers.
Catalog artefacts (GDSN trade-item records, datasheets, images, classification assignments) and master-data quality, provenance, access and identifier retention.
out_of_scope: Serialised physical item instances, SGTIN, serial numbers, GRAI/GIAI assets and SSCC logistic units (sibling instance / logistics models, especially WM-OBJ-001).
Batch/lot, consumer product variant as a subclass identifier, and expiry/manufacture dates of a specific production run (sub-class, not class).
Commercial offers, prices, currency, stock availability, shipping, returns policy as a seller promise, and marketplace listings (schema.org/Offer / GoodRelations Offer).
Engineering BOM structure, quantities and effectivity as a composition graph (WM-OBJ-019 composes this type; the BOM itself is out of scope).
Organisations, locations (GLN), parties, contracts, purchase orders, invoices and EPCIS instance events as first-class entities.
Instance-level country-of-assembly when it varies by plant or lot, and operator-specific inventory positions.
Digital Product Passport instance payloads, patient-level UDI production identifiers, and coupon/restricted GS1 prefixes that are not trade-item types.

boundary_notes.distinction: This model is the class: all occurrences share the same class-level GS1 identifier (GTIN) and inherited master data. WM-OBJ-001 is the instance: GTIN plus serial (SGTIN) with data not inherited upward. Schema.org IndividualProduct and FDA UDI production identifiers (lot, serial, expiry) belong on the instance, not here.

A catalog item is the thing that may be priced, ordered or invoiced; an Offer is a time-bounded transfer of rights (sell, lease, repair) with price, availability and eligible region. GoodRelations and schema.org keep Product/ProductModel separate from Offer. Price, InStock and seller terms must not be stored as type master data.

An engineering BOM composes component product types (this model) with quantities and structure. This model records that a type may be a component or an assembly type; it does not hold BOM lines, effectivity or substitute-part rules.

ProductGroup is a prototype for variants that differ only on named dimensions and is not itself offered for sale. ProductModel is a datasheet/prototypical description, possibly with predecessorOf/successorOf. A catalog item with its own GTIN is a trade item, not merely a group template. GMN identifies a product model/family and SHALL NOT replace GTIN.
GTIN plus batch/lot or consumer product variant is sub-class granularity. Class-level catalog items must not embed lot, serial or expiry in their primary identifier or Digital Link path.

sources.title: Global Trade Item Number (GTIN)
sources.relevance: Defines GTIN as the GS1 key for any trade item that may be priced, ordered or invoiced, and points to General Specifications and the GTIN Management Standard as governing assignment.

sources.title: GTIN Management Standard, Release 1.1, Ratified
sources.relevance: Normative rules for when a new GTIN is required (new product, formulation/functionality, net content, dimensions, certification mark, brand, promotional item, pack quantity, assortment, price-on-pack) and that local regulation supersedes the GS1 minimum.

sources.title: schema.org Product
sources.relevance: Web-scale product type with GTIN/MPN/SKU/brand, measurements, certifications, variant and accessory relations; also the contested overlap with Offer via the offers property.

sources.title: schema.org ProductModel
sources.relevance: Datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product; isVariantOf, predecessorOf and successorOf model type-level lineage without treating the model as a serialised instance.

sources.title: schema.org Offer
sources.relevance: Defines the offer as transfer of rights with price, availability and businessFunction; itemOffered points at Product. Establishes the type-versus-offer boundary this model must not collapse.

sources.title: schema.org IndividualProduct
sources.relevance: A single identifiable product instance with serialNumber; Digital Link guidance forbids attaching AI 21 serial URIs to class-level Product/ProductModel.

sources.title: GS1 Digital Link Standard: URI Syntax
sources.relevance: Canonical HTTPS URI for class-level GTIN (AI 01 as 14 digits), GMN (AI 8013), and hierarchical qualifiers; serial and lot are key qualifiers, not class keys. Canonical host id.gs1.org.

sources.title: UDI Basics
sources.version_or_date: page current as of 2026-08-23; UDI Rule 78 FR 58826, 2013-09-24
sources.relevance: Splits UDI into Device Identifier (version/model, submitted to GUDID) versus Production Identifier (lot, serial, expiry, manufacture date). DI is the regulated type key; PI is instance/sub-class and out of this model.

sources.title: GS1 General Specifications Change Notification WR 24-004 — Global Model Number (GMN) and medical device family
sources.version_or_date: GS1 General Specifications Release 24.0, ratified January 2024
sources.relevance: GMN identifies a product model/family, SHALL NOT identify a trade item, SHALL NOT be reissued, and maps to EU Basic UDI-DI. Brand owner owns both GMN and GTIN. GTIN SHALL associate with at most one GMN.

sources.title: ISO 22745-1:2010 Industrial automation systems and integration — Open technical dictionaries and their application to master data — Part 1: Overview and fundamental principles
sources.relevance: Architecture for cataloguing items as class-plus-property-value master data via an open technical dictionary and identification guide, satisfying ISO 8000-110 characteristic-data exchange.

sources.title: IEC 61360-2:2012 Standard data element types with associated classification scheme for electric components — Part 2: EXPRESS dictionary schema
sources.relevance: Formal dictionary model separating characterization class from categorization class; classes are abstractions of product sets sharing properties. Basis of IEC CDD and eCl@ss.

sources.title: GS1 Global Product Classification (GPC) Browser
sources.relevance: Authoritative four-level retail classification (Segment/Family/Class/Brick plus brick attributes). One brick per GTIN; many GTINs per brick. Mandated category method for GDSN.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Provenance of catalog master-data records: entities, activities, agents, generation and derivation, so type records can separate event time from ingestion time and attribute stewardship.

sources.title: schema.org ProductGroup
sources.relevance: Variant group that is not directly offered; variesBy, hasVariant and productGroupID distinguish size/colour/material siblings that each have their own trade-item identity.

sources.title: GS1 Traceability Standard (GTS2) — identification granularity (class, batch/lot, instance)
sources.version_or_date: ratified PDF, document dated 2019-09-05 on published file
sources.relevance: Explicit class-level GTIN versus GTIN+lot versus GTIN+serial. Class-level data examples: product name, ingredients, nutritional information, net content, packaging dimensions.

sources.title: Can a GTIN be re-used?
sources.version_or_date: policy effective after December 2018 / 1 January 2019; article cites General Specifications section 4.17.1
sources.relevance: After 2018 a GTIN allocated to a trade item SHALL NOT be reallocated, with narrow never-produced and unmodified-reintroduction exceptions; underpins retention of retired catalog identifiers.

sources.title: UNSPSC — How UNSPSC Differs from GPC
sources.relevance: States there is no official mapping between UNSPSC (procurement spend) and GPC (retail/GDSN). Prevents treating one classification as a substitute for the other.

sources.title: WCO Harmonized System Classification Handbook
sources.version_or_date: handbook describing HS structure; HS 2022 nomenclature in force for international trade
sources.relevance: HS is the customs/statistical goods nomenclature (4-digit headings, 5/6-digit subheadings, national extensions). Type-level tariff classification is distinct from GPC/UNSPSC.

sources.title: ISO 8000-110:2021 Data quality — Part 110: Master data: Exchange of characteristic data: Syntax, semantic encoding, and conformance to data specification
sources.relevance: Computer-checkable requirements for exchanging item characteristic master data against a data specification and encoded dictionary; companion to ISO 22745 catalogues.

bundles.name: Identity and identification keys
bundles.description: Class-level identity of a catalog item: the authoritative trade-item key, auxiliary type keys, and governed IRIs. Serial, lot and offer identifiers are excluded.
bundles.rationale: Agents cannot operate a catalog without a unique class key, a checkable encoding, an allocator, and a clear prohibition on using instance or commercial identifiers as the type key.

layers.name: Class-level trade item key
layers.description: GTIN as the globally unique class identifier for a trade item, including format, check digit, packaging-level uniqueness and Digital Link encoding without qualifiers.

findings.name: GTIN as class-level catalog identity
findings.description: A GTIN uniquely identifies a trade item class (product or service that may be priced, ordered or invoiced). Class-level marking does not distinguish two occurrences of the same type. Each packaging level that moves in the supply chain requires its own GTIN. GTIN-8/12/13/14 are encodings of one key; Digital Link requires 14-digit expression with leading zeros.

questions.text: What is the authoritative class-level GTIN for this catalog item, in which encoding (GTIN-8, GTIN-12, GTIN-13 or GTIN-14), and which issuing GS1 Company Prefix allocated it?
Does this identifier identify the class of all identical trade items rather than a serialised instance, lot, logistic unit or restricted-circulation number?
Which packaging hierarchy level does this GTIN identify (base consumer unit, inner pack, case, pallet trade item) and what are the sibling GTINs at other levels?
What is the canonical GS1 Digital Link URI for this class (HTTPS, 14-digit AI 01, no serial/lot/CPV path) and is it the id.gs1.org form or a brand-owner resolver URI?

data_elements.name: GTIN
data_elements.description: Numeric GS1 Global Trade Item Number uniquely identifying the trade-item class. Store native length plus a 14-digit zero-padded canonical form; do not treat left-padding as a different item.

data_elements.name: GTIN encoding
data_elements.description: Declared encoding used on pack or in messages: GTIN-8, GTIN-12, GTIN-13 or GTIN-14.

data_elements.name: Canonical GS1 Digital Link URI
data_elements.description: HTTPS URI encoding only the class GTIN (AI 01, 14 digits). Must not include AI 10, 21 or 22 for this model.

data_elements.name: Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID
data_elements.description: Local governed identifier assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master-system GTIN or IRI exists yet. A date is not an identifier.

artifacts.name: GTIN allocation record
artifacts.description: Brand-owner record of Company Prefix, item reference, check digit, packaging level and allocation timestamp for this class.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative GTIN in the allocator's GS1 system first; then canonical Digital Link IRI; then Dimension UUID/ULID.

findings.name: Auxiliary type identifiers
findings.description: Manufacturer Part Number with brand, merchant SKU, marketplace ASIN, NATO stock number, ISBN and GMN identify the type in other namespaces. None of these replace GTIN for open-supply-chain trade items. SKU is merchant-specific; MPN is manufacturer-specific; GMN is a model/family key, not a trade-item key.

questions.text: What manufacturer part number and brand jointly identify this type when a GTIN is absent or as a secondary key?
Which merchant SKU, ASIN or other catalog keys exist, who assigned each, and in which catalog namespace are they unique?
Is there a Global Model Number or other model/family identifier, and does each GTIN associate with at most one GMN?

data_elements.name: Manufacturer part number
data_elements.description: Manufacturer-assigned type identifier; uniqueness is within brand/manufacturer, not global.

data_elements.name: Stock keeping unit
data_elements.description: Merchant-specific type identifier for the catalog item or the product to which an offer refers; not a global class key.

data_elements.name: Global Model Number
data_elements.description: GS1 AI 8013 product-model/family identifier. Must not be used as a trade-item identifier. Once assigned SHALL NOT be reissued to another model.

data_elements.name: Amazon Standard Identification Number
data_elements.description: Marketplace type identifier; not a GS1 key. Record as text or URL per schema.org.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Auxiliary keys are identifiers and namespace metadata stored on the catalog-item record; they are not independent serial artefacts unless a third-party registry extract is retained as evidence.

bundles.name: Classification and characteristic dictionaries
bundles.description: How the catalog item is placed in retail, procurement, customs and industrial class systems, and how its properties are encoded against a dictionary rather than free text.
bundles.rationale: Identification keys do not support category analysis or semantic comparison across manufacturers. Classification and dictionary-coded properties are the interoperable description layer.

layers.name: Multi-scheme classification
layers.description: GPC brick for GDSN/retail, UNSPSC commodity for procurement, HS code for customs, and IEC/eCl@ss characterization class for industrial catalogues. Schemes are not interchangeable and have no official crosswalk.

findings.name: Classification scheme assignments
findings.description: A catalog item may carry many classifications. GPC assigns exactly one brick per GTIN; the brick may have mutually exclusive attributes. UNSPSC is four-level (Segment/Family/Class/Commodity) for spend. HS is a 6-digit international goods code with national extensions. GPC is limited to tradeable physical goods in its retail design; UNSPSC covers goods and services.

questions.text: What GPC Segment, Family, Class and Brick (and brick attribute values) classify this GTIN in the version of GPC used for GDSN?
What UNSPSC commodity code and Harmonized System heading/subheading (plus any national tariff extension) apply, and for which process (procurement versus customs)?
Which classification schemes are intentionally absent because they are out of industry scope (for example GPC on a pure service) and who decided that?
Is any mapping between GPC, UNSPSC, HS or eCl@ss asserted, and if so is it an official correspondence or a local heuristic?

data_elements.name: GPC brick code
data_elements.description: Eight-digit GPC brick uniquely categorising the trade item for GDSN. One brick per GTIN.

data_elements.name: UNSPSC code
data_elements.description: Eight-digit (optional ten-digit) procurement classification.

data_elements.name: Harmonized System code
data_elements.description: WCO HS heading/subheading used for customs and trade statistics; may include national digits beyond six.

data_elements.name: Classification scheme version
data_elements.description: Published version or release date of the classification codeset used.

artifacts.name: Classification assignment record
artifacts.description: Versioned assignment of one or more scheme codes to the catalog item, with classifier identity and codeset version.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Catalog-item GTIN or Dimension UUID plus scheme URI and codeset version.

layers.name: Dictionary-encoded characteristic properties
layers.description: ISO 22745/8000 and IEC 61360 treat a catalogue item as a class plus property-value pairs drawn from an open technical dictionary, not as unconstrained text.

findings.name: Characteristic data against a dictionary
findings.description: Master data describing the item is a set of dictionary-identified properties with values, units and constraints that can be computer-checked for syntax, semantic encoding and conformance to a data specification (identification guide). Dictionaries (IEC CDD, eCl@ss, eOTD) must not be confused with the catalogue itself.

questions.text: Which characterization or categorization class in which dictionary (IRDI or equivalent) does this catalog item instantiate?
Which properties are mandatory in the identification guide or application class, and which observed values with units satisfy them?
Does the exchanged characteristic-data message conform to ISO 8000-110 syntax, semantic encoding and the cited data specification?

data_elements.name: Dictionary class identifier
data_elements.description: IRDI or URI of the characterization/categorization class in IEC 61360, eCl@ss or an ISO 22745 OTD.

data_elements.name: Property-value set
data_elements.description: Collection of dictionary properties with values, units and constraints describing the type.

data_elements.name: Data specification / identification guide
data_elements.description: Identifier of the ISO 22745 identification guide or ISO 8000 data specification the record claims to satisfy.

artifacts.name: Identification-guide conformance report
artifacts.description: Machine-checkable result of validating characteristic data against the cited data specification.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Catalog-item identifier plus data-specification version and validation timestamp.

bundles.name: Type specification and declared attributes
bundles.description: Human and machine descriptions that apply identically to every occurrence of the class: names, brand, language, net content, formulation, dimensions and type-level measurements.
bundles.rationale: GS1 class-level data and schema.org Product/ProductModel properties are the operational content of a catalog item once identity is fixed.

layers.name: Naming, brand and language
layers.description: Trade item descriptions, brand ownership of the specification, and language-specific packaging as a potential GTIN-change driver.

findings.name: Names, brand and intended audience
findings.description: A catalog item has a consumer/trading-partner distinguished name, optional additional descriptions, a brand (organization or Brand), manufacturer, and intended audience. A Spanish-only packaging of an English product is a new product requiring a new GTIN. Primary brand change requires a new GTIN.

questions.text: What are the governed short and long names of this catalog item, in which languages, and which name is canonical for trading-partner exchange?
Which brand and manufacturer organisations are associated with this type, and is the brand owner the GTIN allocator?
Has language-only packaging or a primary brand change occurred such that trading partners must distinguish a new GTIN?

data_elements.name: Canonical name
data_elements.description: Primary trade-item name used in catalogs and GDSN description fields.

data_elements.name: Brand
data_elements.description: Brand associated with the product type.

data_elements.name: Manufacturer
data_elements.description: Organisation that manufactures the type; may differ from brand owner.

data_elements.name: Description
data_elements.description: Human-readable type description; not a substitute for dictionary-coded properties.

artifacts.name: Product datasheet / ProductModel specification
artifacts.description: Vendor specification of the prototypical product, possibly multilingual, corresponding to schema.org ProductModel.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Prefer GTIN or GMN IRI; else ProductModel URL; else Dimension UUID.

layers.name: Declared physical and functional attributes
layers.description: Net content, formulation/functionality, dimensional/gross-weight bands, and type-level measurements that both describe the class and trigger GTIN change when legally declared information changes.

findings.name: Declared net content, formulation and type measurements
findings.description: Class-level data inherited by all instances includes product name, ingredients, nutritional information, net content and packaging dimensions. Changes to declared formulation/functionality that affect legally required pack information and that the brand owner expects partners to distinguish require a new GTIN. Schema.org hasMeasurement, height/width/depth/weight capture type-level quantities, including ranges for adjustable products.

questions.text: What declared net content, dimensions, weight and other type-level measurements apply, with units and whether each is a point value or a range?
What declared formulation, ingredients or functionality define this type, and which of those declarations are legally required on pack?
Would a proposed change to net content, dimensions, gross weight, formulation or functionality require a new GTIN under the GTIN Management Standard and any stricter local regulation?
What country of origin, assembly or last processing is declared at type level, and is it actually invariant across plants and lots?

data_elements.name: Declared net content
data_elements.description: Net content as declared for the trade item, with unit of measure.

data_elements.name: Type-level measurements
data_elements.description: Height, width, depth, weight and other hasMeasurement quantities for the class, including ranges.

data_elements.name: Country of origin
data_elements.description: Declared country of origin of the product type; interpretation varies by context and may not be invariant.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Declared quantities and formulation statements are characteristic master data on the catalog item; they become artefacts only when a labelled pack facsimile or regulated nutrition/ingredient document is retained.

bundles.name: Variants, models and packaging hierarchy
bundles.description: How one product family fans out into orderable GTINs (size/colour/material and pack levels) without collapsing those GTINs into a single offer or a single instance.
bundles.rationale: Each style/colour/size and each packaging level is a unique product requiring its own GTIN; ProductGroup/ProductModel express the family without being the trade item.

layers.name: Variant groups and product models
layers.description: ProductGroup templates, ProductModel datasheets, isVariantOf inheritance and predecessor/successor lineage.

findings.name: Variant grouping and model lineage
findings.description: A ProductGroup represents products that vary only in well-described ways (size, colour, material) and is not itself sold. Variants inherit group features unless overridden; isVariantOf is not transitive. ProductModel adds predecessorOf/successorOf for discontinued-to-newer model pointers. Each sellable variant that trading partners must distinguish still needs its own GTIN (jeans size example in GTIN Management Standard).

questions.text: Which product group or base model does this catalog item belong to, and which dimensions (variesBy) distinguish its siblings?
What sibling catalog items (GTINs) share the group, and which features are inherited versus locally overridden?
Which product models are predecessor or successor of this type, and was the predecessor discontinued?

data_elements.name: Product group identifier
data_elements.description: Parent SKU or productGroupID for the variant family.

data_elements.name: Varies-by dimensions
data_elements.description: Properties that distinguish variants in the group (size, colour, material, etc.).

data_elements.name: Is variant of
data_elements.description: Reference to ProductGroup or ProductModel from which this type inherits.

data_elements.name: Predecessor / successor model
data_elements.description: Type-level lineage pointers among ProductModels.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Variant grouping is a set of typed references among catalog items; a separate artefact is needed only if a family datasheet or visual variant matrix is published.

layers.name: Packaging hierarchy of trade items
layers.description: Unique GTIN per packaging level that is ordered, invoiced or scanned as a trade item, distinct from SSCC logistic units.

findings.name: Packaging-level GTIN hierarchy
findings.description: GTIN is assigned at the retail consumer trade item (base unit) and a unique GTIN at every higher packaging level used in distribution. New product introduction requires new GTINs at base and higher levels. Pack/case quantity changes have their own GTIN Management rule. Logistic units use SSCC and are out of scope.

questions.text: What is the base consumer-unit GTIN and how many of those units are contained in each higher-level trade-item GTIN?
Has pack or case quantity changed such that a new higher-level GTIN is mandatory while the base unit may remain?
Is this catalog item a predefined assortment or bundle of other catalog items, and which child GTINs and quantities does it contain?

data_elements.name: Packaging level
data_elements.description: Code for base unit, inner pack, case, pallet trade item or equivalent.

data_elements.name: Contained quantity
data_elements.description: Count of next-lower trade items contained in this packaging level.

data_elements.name: Child trade items
data_elements.description: References to contained catalog items for cases, inner packs and predefined assortments.

artifacts.name: Packaging hierarchy record
artifacts.description: Bill of packaging linking GTINs and quantities across trade-item levels, distinct from an engineering BOM.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each node identified by its GTIN; the hierarchy artefact identified by base-unit GTIN plus version timestamp.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, ownership and authority
bundles.description: Who may mint, change and retire a catalog item, under which rules, and how identifiers persist after withdrawal.
bundles.rationale: GTIN assignment, change and non-reuse are the operating surface for catalog stewardship; brand owner (GTIN allocator) is the authority, not the warehouse.

layers.name: Assignment and GTIN change
layers.description: New-product versus replacement-product decisions and the ten GTIN Management rules plus local legal overrides.

findings.name: GTIN assignment and change rules
findings.description: New products always receive a new GTIN at every hierarchy level. Replacement products change GTIN when formulation/functionality (with both legal declaration and distinguishability), declared net content, dimensional/gross-weight thresholds, certification marks, primary brand, time-critical promotions, pack quantity, predefined assortment or price-on-pack rules fire. At least one guiding principle (distinguishability, regulatory disclosure, supply-chain impact) must apply. Brand owners may change GTIN more often than the minimum. The standard SHALL NOT be used to identify non-new (used) trade items.

questions.text: Is this catalog item a new product (not previously in the brand owner's portfolio) or a change to an existing in-market product?
Which GTIN Management rules and guiding principles fired for this version, and did any local regulation require a stricter change?
When was the GTIN assigned (event time) versus when was that assignment ingested into this Dimension (observation time)?
Is this record being used to identify a non-new, refurbished or returned trade item, which this standard forbids?

data_elements.name: Catalog lifecycle status
data_elements.description: Draft, investigational, active, withdrawn, discontinued or deleted, aligned with GS1 catalogue statuses that affect reuse exceptions.

data_elements.name: GTIN change rationale
data_elements.description: Rules and guiding principles that justified assignment or change.

data_elements.name: Assignment event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when the allocator assigned the GTIN, with offset or Z.

artifacts.name: GTIN change decision record
artifacts.description: Steward decision capturing old/new GTIN, rules fired, regulation override and timestamps.

layers.name: Retirement, non-reuse and allocator authority
layers.description: Discontinuation, identifier persistence, never-produced exceptions, and the brand-owner/labeler who is accountable.

findings.name: Identifier non-reuse, discontinuation and GTIN allocator
findings.description: From 1 January 2019 an allocated GTIN SHALL NOT be reallocated to another trade item. Exceptions: never-produced draft GTINs after 12 months and partner agreement; unmodified reintroduction of a withdrawn item. Healthcare and directly marked technical parts already forbade reuse. Brand owner owns the specifications of the trade item and is normally the GTIN allocator; device labeler (often manufacturer) owns UDI-DI submission. GMN SHALL NOT be reissued.

questions.text: Who is the GTIN allocator / brand owner, who is the manufacturer or device labeler if different, and under which GS1 Company Prefix or FDA-accredited issuing agency was the type key issued?
Has this GTIN been withdrawn, was it ever produced, and is reuse forbidden or limited to a documented exception?
Which roles may create, patch or mark-deleted this catalog item, and is hard deletion of an allocated GTIN prohibited in favour of discontinued status?
Which agent generated or revised this master-data entity, through which activity, and what prior entity was it derived from?

data_elements.name: GTIN allocator / brand owner
data_elements.description: Party that owns the trade-item specification and allocated the GTIN.

data_elements.name: Identifier reuse policy
data_elements.description: Non-reuse rule plus any never-produced or reintroduction exception recorded for this key.

data_elements.name: Discontinued at
data_elements.description: Event time when the type was withdrawn from the catalog, RFC 3339.

artifacts.name: Discontinuation or withdrawal notice
artifacts.description: Notice to trading partners that a GTIN is withdrawn, with instruction not to reallocate.

bundles.name: Regulatory type identifiers, certification and catalog evidence
bundles.description: Type-level regulated identifiers (UDI-DI, Basic UDI-DI/GMN), certification marks that can force GTIN change, and the catalog artefacts that evidence the type.
bundles.rationale: Regulated healthcare and certification marks are first-class type concerns; GDSN/GUDID records are the operational evidence an agent must read and write.

layers.name: Regulated type identifiers and marks
layers.description: FDA UDI Device Identifier versus production identifiers; EU Basic UDI-DI via GMN; certification marks on pack.

findings.name: UDI-DI, Basic UDI-DI and type-level certifications
findings.description: For medical devices the Device Identifier identifies labeler plus version/model and is the GUDID key; production identifiers stay off this model. EU Basic UDI-DI is implemented as GMN and is assigned independently of packaging; GTIN (UDI-DI) remains the supply-chain trade-item key. Adding or removing a certification mark that trading partners must distinguish requires a new GTIN. Schema.org hasCertification records issuer, name and rating or identification.

questions.text: If this type is a medical device, what is the UDI Device Identifier (and issuing agency) and the Basic UDI-DI/GMN, and are production identifiers excluded from this record?
Which certifications, marks or energy classes apply at type level, who issued them, and did add/remove of a mark require a new GTIN?
What GUDID or equivalent registry fields (brand name, version/model, GMDN, package count, premarket number) are bound to this type?
Does an FDA UDI exception, alternative or other regional exemption apply so that this type has no UDI-DI?

data_elements.name: UDI Device Identifier
data_elements.description: Fixed portion of UDI identifying labeler and version/model; GUDID key. Not a production identifier.

data_elements.name: Basic UDI-DI
data_elements.description: Medical-device family identifier, represented in GS1 as GMN; independent of packaging.

data_elements.name: Type-level certifications
data_elements.description: Certification objects (issuer, name, identification or rating) that apply to all instances of the type.

artifacts.name: GUDID / UDI database device record
artifacts.description: Published device-identifier master data for a version/model; excludes production identifiers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: UDI-DI as master-system identifier; Basic UDI-DI/GMN as family IRI.

layers.name: Catalog artefacts, quality and access
layers.description: GDSN trade-item messages, images, datasheets, validation and who may read or export them.

findings.name: Catalog publication, quality and access
findings.description: A catalog item is published as master data (GDSN/GUDID/web ProductModel), optionally with images and media. Quality is judged by ISO 8000-110 checkability and GS1 check-digit/prefix validity. Access defaults to trading-partner or public catalog rules; adult-oriented and regulated types need scoped exceptions. Provenance uses PROV agents and generation times. Offers nested under schema.org Product must be stored in an offer model, not here.

questions.text: In which catalogs, data pools or public pages is this type published, under which identifier, and what is the publication status?
What check-digit, prefix, dictionary-conformance and completeness evidence supports this record, and when was it last validated?
Who may read, export or patch this catalog item at bundle, layer, finding and artefact scope, and which adult, investigational or confidential exceptions apply?
How long must the identifier and master data be retained after discontinuation so that non-reuse and traceability are preserved?

data_elements.name: Publication channels
data_elements.description: GDSN pool, GUDID, public ProductModel URL or internal MDM publication targets.

data_elements.name: Validation result
data_elements.description: Latest computer-checkable validation of GTIN syntax and characteristic-data conformance.

data_elements.name: Record generation time
data_elements.description: PROV generation time of this master-data entity (observation/ingestion), distinct from business event time.

artifacts.name: GDSN trade item master-data message
artifacts.description: Synchronised trade-item attributes for this GTIN, including GPC brick, descriptions and hierarchy, excluding price offers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: GTIN as GDSN key; message id as artefact serial of the publication event, not of the type.

artifacts.name: Product image and media set
artifacts.description: Type-level images and media referenced from the catalog item (pack shots, colour swatches), not instance photographs.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Content hash plus catalog-item GTIN; GDTI may identify the document but is not the product type.

bundles.name: Typed relationships and interoperability alignments
bundles.description: How this classifier links to instances, BOMs, accessories and external vocabularies without absorbing those neighbours.
bundles.rationale: The registry default link type is TYPED-EDGES; classifies-instances and BOM composition are already candidate relations and must stay explicit.

layers.name: Neighbor model and vocabulary links
layers.description: Classifies instances, is composed by engineering BOM, accessory/spare/similar/consumable edges, and alignments to GS1, schema.org, ISO/IEC and FDA.

findings.name: Type-instance classification and sibling product edges
findings.description: This catalog item classifies zero or more item instances (WM-OBJ-001). It may be a component type in an engineering BOM (WM-OBJ-019). Schema.org provides isAccessoryOrSparePartFor, isConsumableFor, isRelatedTo and isSimilarTo at type level. Offers use itemOffered toward this type and must not be stored as edges of the type itself. Interoperability is alignment, not claimed conformance.

questions.text: Which item-instance records (serialised or otherwise) does this catalog item classify, and is the edge always class-to-instance rather than lot-to-instance?
Which engineering BOMs list this catalog item as a component or assembly type, and at what quantity at the type level?
Which other catalog items are declared accessories, spares, consumables, related or similar, and in which direction?
Which external vocabularies is this record aligned to (schema.org ProductModel, GS1 trade item, ISO 22745 item, IEC 61360 class, FDA DI), and what conflicts are recorded rather than hidden?

data_elements.name: Classifies instances
data_elements.description: Typed edges from this product type to WM-OBJ-001 item instances.

data_elements.name: Related product edges
data_elements.description: Accessory, spare, consumable, similar and related type-to-type references.

data_elements.name: External alignment set
data_elements.description: Declared alignments to GS1, schema.org, ISO/IEC and regulatory type identifiers with conflict notes.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Typed edges and alignment declarations are reference data on the catalog item; neighbour models hold their own artefacts (instance records, BOM files, offer documents).

functions.name: Assign class-level catalog key
functions.description: Allocate a GTIN (or interim Dimension UUID plus MPN/brand) to a new catalog item at a stated packaging level, recording allocator, event time and ingestion time.
preconditions: Allocator is the brand owner or authorised GTIN allocator.
Item is a new product or a replacement that has already been judged to need a new GTIN.
Key is not a serial, lot, SSCC or offer identifier.
effects: Creates a catalog-item master record at class granularity.
Registers non-reuse obligation on the allocated key.

functions.name: Evaluate whether a type change requires a new GTIN
functions.description: Apply GTIN Management rules and any stricter local regulation to a proposed attribute change and either keep the GTIN or mint a successor.
preconditions: Current item is an existing in-market or previously assigned type.
Change is not an attempt to identify a used/non-new item.
effects: May create a successor catalog item and predecessorOf/successorOf links.
Leaves a decision artefact for audit.

functions.name: Classify catalog item in one or more schemes
functions.description: Assign GPC brick (exactly one if GDSN), optional UNSPSC, HS and dictionary class/property values, recording codeset versions.
preconditions: Selected schemes are applicable (GPC not forced onto pure services).
effects: Updates classification edges without claiming unofficial crosswalks as official.

functions.name: Publish catalog item master data
functions.description: Emit GDSN/GUDID/ProductModel publication of type master data without embedding Offer price or availability.
preconditions: Required identity and description fields present.
GTIN check digit and prefix validity pass if GTIN present.
Offer/price fields are absent or stripped.
effects: Makes type data available to trading partners or public consumers.
Records PROV generation of the published entity.

functions.name: Retire catalog item without recycling the key
functions.description: Mark a type discontinued/withdrawn, notify partners, retain the identifier tombstone, and block reallocation except documented never-produced exceptions.
preconditions: If reuse is requested, never-produced and partner-agreement tests must pass.
effects: Identifier remains reserved; master data retained per policy.

functions.name: Validate catalog item identity and characteristic data
functions.description: Computer-check GTIN length/check digit/prefix, Digital Link syntax, dictionary encoding and identification-guide conformance.
preconditions: Record is readable at finding scope.
effects: Attaches a quality evidence object; does not by itself change lifecycle status.

functions.name: Resolve class-level Digital Link
functions.description: Parse a GS1 Digital Link URI, reject serial/lot/CPV-qualified URIs as out of this model, and bind the 14-digit GTIN or GMN to the catalog item.
preconditions: URI is syntactically a GS1 Digital Link per URI Syntax 1.7.0.
effects: Either binds to an existing type or rejects toward instance/lot handling.

functions.name: Link type to instances or BOM composition
functions.description: Create typed edges CLASSIFIES to item instances or accept COMPOSE from an engineering BOM without copying instance or BOM payloads into this model.
preconditions: Target exists in the neighbour model.
Relation is CLASSIFIES, accessory/spare/similar, or BOM composition — not Offer.

composition.purpose: This catalog item CLASSIFIES item instances; instances hold serial/lot/SGTIN and must not be stored here.
An engineering BOM COMPOSE-s this product type as a component or assembly type; BOM structure stays in WM-OBJ-019.
Align prototypical datasheet semantics, isVariantOf inheritance and predecessorOf/successorOf lineage without claiming schema.org conformance of every record.
Align variant-family templates (variesBy/hasVariant) that are not themselves trade items.
Offers point at this type via itemOffered; price and availability remain in the offer model.

composition.target: GS1 GTIN / GPC / GDSN trade item
composition.purpose: Primary open-supply-chain identity, retail classification and master-data synchronisation for trade-item types.

composition.target: GS1 Global Model Number / Basic UDI-DI
composition.purpose: Optional model/family identifier above GTIN, required in regulated healthcare as Basic UDI-DI, never a GTIN substitute.
US regulated type key for device version/model; production identifiers excluded.
Characteristic-data catalogue and quality-exchange alignment for dictionary-coded type descriptions.
Industrial product-class and property dictionary alignment.
Customs/statistical goods classification of the type, independent of GPC/UNSPSC.
Provenance mixin for generation, derivation and agents on catalog master-data records.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the steward organisation that acts as brand owner or catalog steward for this Dimension's WM-OBJ-002 records.
Declare whether GS1 Company Prefix allocation, FDA-accredited UDI issuance, or local UUID/ULID is the master identity system.
Provide AGENTS.md plus Specification, Storage type, Interface and Processes URLs before agents write catalog items.
Record jurisdiction(s) whose labelling/UDI/GTIN-change regulations override GS1 minima.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Prefer the allocator's GTIN (canonical 14-digit form and Digital Link IRI on id.gs1.org or the brand resolver) as the master identifier; use GMN/UDI-DI as additional governed IRIs; assign a Dimension UUID/ULID only when no master-system key exists. Do not use dates, SKUs or offer IDs as the catalog-item primary key.
registry_links: vr.wm-obj-002 / WM-OBJ-002 Product Type / Catalog Item
GS1 GTIN, GPC, GDSN and Digital Link
schema.org Product, ProductModel, ProductGroup, Offer, IndividualProduct

canonicalization_rules: Canonical GTIN is 14 digits with leading zeros; native GTIN-8/12/13 is retained as encoding metadata, not as a second item.
Canonical Digital Link for this model contains only AI 01 (or AI 8013 for GMN) and no AI 10/21/22 path segments.
Names and descriptions are language-tagged; one canonical name per catalog locale policy.
Classification codes are stored with scheme URI and codeset version; unofficial crosswalks are labelled heuristic.
Offer, price, inventory and serial/lot fields present in inbound schema.org Product payloads are stripped or redirected to neighbour models.
patch_rules: Patches that would violate a fired GTIN Management rule must either be rejected or spawn a successor catalog item with a new GTIN.
Identifier fields (GTIN, GMN, UDI-DI) are immutable after allocation except for documented never-produced deletion.
Status may move to withdrawn/discontinued but allocated keys remain as tombstones.
Characteristic-data patches must re-run ISO 8000-style validation against the cited data specification.
compatibility_rules: Alignments to GS1, schema.org, ISO/IEC and FDA are projections; a record may be valid in this model while incomplete for GDSN or GUDID publication.
Schema.org Product that nests Offer remains interoperable only if Offer is stored separately.
Historical GTINs reused before 2019 may exist; treat as conflicted identity, not as a licence to reuse again.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier (GTIN in GS1/GDSN, UDI-DI in GUDID, GMN in UDI registration) when present.
Governed global identifier/IRI (canonical GS1 Digital Link, schema.org ProductModel URL, dictionary IRDI).
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master key exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All assignment, discontinuation, publication, validation and provenance times SHALL be RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; record business event time and observation/ingestion time separately when they differ.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Artefacts of a type (datasheet, GDSN message, image set, decision record) are not serialised products; name them {gtin-or-uuid}-{artefact-kind}-{event-time} and never encode instance serials into type artefact names.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Persist a checksum of each published artefact payload; GTIN values must pass the GS1 check-digit algorithm and must not use restricted or coupon prefixes.

policies: Class versus instance versus offer: a WM-OBJ-002 record MUST NOT store serial numbers, lot/expiry production identifiers, SSCC, or seller price/availability as if they were type master data.
GTIN and GMN non-reuse: allocated class keys SHALL NOT be recycled except the documented never-produced exception; discontinued types remain queryable tombstones.
Regulatory floor: local legal GTIN-change, labelling and UDI rules supersede GS1 and schema.org minima.
Master-data quality: characteristic data exchanged across organisations SHOULD be dictionary-encoded and computer-checkable per ISO 8000-110/ISO 22745 when an identification guide exists.

read: Any agent with catalog-read scope may read non-restricted type master data at bundle/layer/finding granularity.
Adult-oriented, investigational and regulated-device types require purpose-limited read scope.
Public Digital Link resolution may return only the class-level link set, never production identifiers.
create: Only the brand owner / GTIN allocator or delegated catalog steward may create a catalog item.
Create MUST run assign-class-key and validate-type-record.
Create MUST set lifecycle status (draft versus active) and PROV generation metadata.
update: Stewards may patch descriptions, classifications and measurements in place only when GTIN Management rules do not require a new key.
Identity keys are immutable after allocation.
Updates that fire change rules MUST create a successor type rather than overwrite the GTIN.
delete: Hard delete of an allocated GTIN/GMN/UDI-DI is forbidden; use discontinued/withdrawn status.
Draft never-produced keys may be deleted only after the 12-month and partner-agreement tests.
Artefact binaries may be purged per media-retention policy; identifier tombstones remain.

roles.name: Brand owner / GTIN allocator
responsibilities: Own trade-item specifications and allocate GTINs and GMNs.
Decide new versus replacement product and fire GTIN Management rules.
Authorise publication to GDSN and Digital Link resolvers.

roles.name: Catalog steward / inventory master-data steward
responsibilities: Maintain the Dimension catalog, classifications and packaging hierarchy.
Ensure class/instance/offer separation in stored records.
Operate CRUD under policy and keep AGENTS.md current.

roles.name: Device labeler / regulatory affairs
responsibilities: Assign UDI-DI and Basic UDI-DI where applicable.
Submit GUDID/EUDAMED type data without production identifiers.
Record UDI exceptions and certification-mark GTIN impacts.

roles.name: Data quality officer
responsibilities: Run check-digit, prefix and ISO 8000/22745 validation.
Block unofficial classification crosswalks from being marked normative.
Retain validation evidence and PROV traces.

roles.name: Trading-partner consumer agent
responsibilities: Resolve class-level Digital Links and consume GDSN type data.
Must not infer stock, price or serial identity from this model.
Escalate granularity mismatches (lot/serial URIs) to instance handling.

access.default_rule: Default deny on investigational, adult-oriented and non-public regulated-device types; default allow on published retail catalog attributes to agents with catalog-read scope.
exceptions: Investigational/draft GTINs shared only with named development partners (reuse exception depends on that restriction).
UDI and certification artefacts may be public via GUDID/AccessGUDID while internal decision records stay steward-only.
Break-glass read of discontinued tombstones for recall/traceability with mandatory audit.
audit_requirements: Log create, identity-key assignment, GTIN-change decisions, status transitions, publication and every exception read with agent, activity, event time and ingestion time.

coverage.claim: Wide-union context model for a product type / catalog item as a class-level trade-item classifier, grounded in GS1 GTIN/GPC/Digital Link/GTIN Management, schema.org Product/ProductModel/ProductGroup/Offer/IndividualProduct, FDA UDI-DI, GS1 GMN/Basic UDI-DI, ISO 22745/8000-110, IEC 61360 and WCO HS, with explicit exclusions of instances, lots and offers. Not a claim of universal completeness or of conformance of any implementation.

checklist.notes: GTIN (native and 14-digit canonical), Digital Link IRI, GMN, UDI-DI, MPN+brand, SKU, ASIN, Dimension UUID/ULID; dates forbidden as identifiers.
New versus replacement product, GTIN Management rules 2.1–2.10, predecessor/successor, draft/active/withdrawn/discontinued.
CLASSIFIES instances, BOM composition reference, accessory/spare/consumable/similar, variant group membership.
Assignment, discontinuation, publication and validation times as RFC 3339 with separate event and ingestion timestamps.
PROV-O agent/activity/generation/derivation on master-data records and publications.
Brand owner as specification owner and GTIN allocator; manufacturer and device labeler distinguished.
GS1 check digit and prefix rules; ISO 8000-110/22745 identification-guide conformance; Digital Link ABNF.
Bundle/layer/finding/artefact scopes, default rule, investigational and regulated exceptions, audit log.
Post-2018 GTIN/GMN non-reuse, never-produced 12-month exception, tombstones instead of hard delete.
Alignments to GS1, schema.org, ISO/IEC, FDA, WCO HS and UNSPSC with conflicts recorded; no false conformance claims.
GPC brick, UNSPSC, HS, IEC 61360/eCl@ss dictionary class; no official crosswalk.
Type-level net content, dimensions, weight and hasMeasurement ranges; change thresholds that force new GTIN.
FDA UDI-DI versus PI; EU Basic UDI-DI as GMN; certification-mark GTIN impact.
Per-level GTINs versus SSCC logistic units; assortments and pack-quantity change rules.
ProductGroup/ProductModel variesBy and non-transitive isVariantOf; each distinguished variant still a GTIN.

known_omissions: EU Digital Product Passport (ESPR) type-versus-instance payloads are emerging and were not fetched as a primary source in this pass.
Consumer Product Variant (AI 22) and variable-measure GTIN indicator 9 are noted in GS1 Digital Link/GTS but not modelled as first-class findings.
ISBN-10 to ISBN-13/GTIN mapping, CAS chemical identifiers and proprietary taxonomies (Google product category, Amazon browse nodes, ETIM) are not specified beyond ASIN.
Made-to-order versus made-to-stock class rules appear in GS1 ID Standard granularity text but were not fully expanded.
National HS extensions, dual-use export controls and dangerous-goods UN numbers as type attributes are likely neighbours, not specified here.
Full ISO 22745/8000 and IEC 61360 texts are paywalled; architecture is taken from official abstracts and freely available companion material.
GS1 Web Vocabulary semantics chapter is still evolving as a separate Digital Link document.
conflicts: schema.org Product permits nested Offer, GTIN-on-Offer and itemCondition, mixing type, offer and sometimes instance semantics; this model treats that as a projection conflict and strips offer/instance fields.

GPC (retail physical goods, one brick per GTIN) versus UNSPSC (procurement goods and services) versus HS (customs) versus IEC 61360 (characterization class) have different purposes and no official mapping.
FDA UDI-DI is packaging-level device version/model in GUDID; EU Basic UDI-DI/GMN is packaging-independent family identity — both are type-level but not equivalent.
GTIN reuse: pre-2019 48-month (30-month apparel) reuse versus post-2018 never-reuse; healthcare and directly marked parts already never-reused. Historical reused GTINs remain in the wild.
schema.org Product includes services (haircut, streamed episode); GPC guidance excludes services and digital products — a type may be valid as GTIN trade-item service and still have no GPC brick.
ISO 22745 'item' can mean a physical object or a concept class; this model uses only the concept/class reading.
ProductGroup is not offered for sale; a catalog item with a GTIN is orderable — do not store a group template as if it were a trade item.
regional_assumptions: GTIN-12/UPC is the common North American encoding; GTIN-13/EAN/JAN elsewhere; both canonicalise to GTIN-14.
FDA UDI/GUDID is United States law; EU MDR Basic UDI-DI via GMN is a separate regime that may apply to the same type.
Local labelling, language, net-content and certification regulations can force GTIN changes beyond the GS1 minimum.
HS 2022 is the international core; national tariff schedules add digits and legal force.
UNSPSC governance moved from GS1 US back toward UNDP; codeset version must be recorded because stewardship changed.
adversarial_checks: Would a serialised laptop (IndividualProduct + AI 21) be incorrectly stored as WM-OBJ-002? Rejected: serial Digital Links and serialNumber are out of scope.
Would an Amazon listing price and InStock flag be stored on the type? Rejected: schema.org Offer is a neighbour; publish-catalog-item strips those fields.
Would a case-pack quantity change keep the case GTIN? Fail: GTIN Management pack/case quantity rule requires a new higher-level GTIN.
Would a discontinued GTIN be reassigned to a new flavour after four years? Fail under current non-reuse (post-2018); only never-produced draft exception applies.
Would GPC brick 10000384 be treated as unique product identity equivalent to GTIN? Fail: many GTINs share a brick; classification is not identification.
Would GMN be used at POS instead of GTIN? Fail: GMN SHALL NOT identify a trade item.
Would a used/refurbished unit be given a new catalog type under GTIN Management? Fail: standard SHALL NOT identify non-new trade items; that is instance condition.
Would unofficial GPC-to-UNSPSC maps be marked as conforming? Fail: GS1/UNSPSC comparison states there are no official mapping tables.
